C55716.observed: Widened on the QA lead's point that this rule applies to every tab, which the requirement bears out - the sentence sits after all the per-record-type scoring and applies to the final score, so it is the shared last step of the ranking. Now proved on THREE tabs, each the same way: two records alike in everything the search matches on, the one listed second changed by a single letter, the change visible in the results afterwards (the proof search saw it), and the changed record still listed second. Suppliers: two named 'ZZTIEV2159 Halloway Brothers', same telephone and address. Customers: 'ZZTIEBREAK Transport Two' and 'ZZTIEBREAK Transport One', same address. Parts: two described 'ZZTIEP1648 Halyard Bushing', part numbers -1 and -2, renamed to 'halyard Bushing'. One shared rule failing in three independent places points at the shared step rather than at any one record type.
C55716.not_observed: Assets could not be proved either way, and the reason is an instrument limit, not a finding: two assets sharing a unit number exist and read identically in the results, but nothing available here will accept a change to one of them. Seven routes were tried and named - repo searched for a recorded recipe (playbook line 822); the refusal read (it names the missing field); both surfaces tried; fresh records seeded through the full create chain; the neighbouring customer feature walked to reach the asset's own screen; the read-back instrument proved to return both records before any negative was written; and the question 'what would make this my fault' answered - through the screen, Make is a required field these records have no value for and the form will not save; behind the screen, the change is refused outright without a VIN and answers with a server error when one is supplied. Jobs, part sales, purchase orders and supplier invoices cannot be tested this way at all: all four carry system-generated numbers, so nothing can be altered without also changing something the ranking scores.
